name: Why is my toilet tank leaking?

mainEntity.name: Why is my toilet tank leaking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Toilet tank leaks often stem from worn-out components inside the tank. Common culprits include a faulty flapper that doesn't seal properly, a loose or corroded tank-to-bowl bolt, or a cracked fill valve. The rubber gasket between the tank and the bowl can also degrade over time, leading to leaks. Sometimes, a hairline crack in the porcelain tank itself can be the cause, though this is less common. Identifying the exact source usually involves a visual inspection of the tank's interior and exterior, looking for drips or constant water flow.
acceptedAnswer.description: Toilet tank leaks are usually caused by worn-out flappers, loose tank bolts, faulty fill valves, or degraded gaskets. A crack in the porcelain is a less common but serious issue.
